correctness.rationale: The definition counts nonempty distinct linear complete returns, allowing overlapping occurrences. Unary powers contribute the two respective maximum run lengths. A nonunary border must match its first transition at different transitions in its two occurrences; this excludes two-run closed factors and forces a two-run border in a four-run factor. Three-run factors are closed only with equal terminal lengths, and their zero-ended families overlap exactly when b=d. For five-run factors a border containing a 1 must center on different full 1-runs, hence requires b=d and both outer zero lengths at most c. Otherwise a unary zero border occurs just twice precisely when both outer lengths equal that border length and exceed c. The summed run counts give the formula. With x=max(u,v), y=min(u,v), the zero-run total is at least 2x+y; substitution in the equal-one-run branch and completing the square give the n^2/8 excess bound, and the unequal branch gives at most (n-1)^2/12. The stated witness yields 8t^2+6t, and padding its final zero run gives the lower limit at all lengths. The equality correction can vanish when u=v=1. The supplied enumeration was inspected, not run: its 9,592 count includes repeated tuples across two loops, and the ten witness checks in lines 45–50 are formula evaluations, not fresh direct counts. The all-parameter proof does not depend on these checks.
